readiness.walletconnect.reason.en: The wallet now shows whether WalletConnect’s verification service confirms which website a connected app really is, and it summarizes token-permit signatures (Permit and Permit2) as a plain spender, amount and expiry. Both are built and tested offline but have not yet been exercised with a live app over the WalletConnect relay, so connecting to apps is not yet cleared for real funds.

readiness.simple-account.reason.en: SimpleAccount is the ERC-4337 sample account. This wallet has only used it on test networks, it cannot sign messages for apps, and Alchemy’s bundler refused to deploy it in testing, so this wallet uses it only on test networks.

readiness.kernel-smart-account.reason.en: The Kernel v3.3 smart account has no published audit for the deployed version, no confirmed bug bounty and no stated support horizon. Until those exist, this wallet uses Kernel accounts only on test networks.

readiness.eip7702-upgrade.reason.en: The upgrade hands your address to Kernel v3.3, whose EIP-7702 changes have no published audit, no confirmed bug bounty and no stated support horizon. Until those exist, this wallet offers the upgrade only on test networks.

readiness.session-keys.reason.en: Session keys rely on Kernel’s permission policies and session signer, which have no published audit. Until an audit covers them, this wallet grants session keys only on test networks.

readiness.passkeys.reason.en: The passkey validator this wallet installs (WebAuthnValidator v0.0.3) has no published audit, and only the app, not the contract, stops a passkey from replacing the account’s owner. Until both are addressed, passkeys work only on test networks.

readiness.guardians.reason.en: The guardian modules have no published audit, and testing found that one guardian can satisfy a two-of-two threshold by repeating its signature and that guardians can sign as the account immediately. Until this is resolved, guardians and guardian recovery work only on test networks.

readiness.owner-rotation.reason.en: Owner changes run on the Kernel v3.3 account, which has no published audit for the deployed version, and afterwards the account can no longer be found from a recovery phrase alone. This wallet offers owner changes only on test networks.

readiness.paymaster.reason.en: Sponsorship is used only by smart accounts, which are limited to test networks, and no live paymaster has been tested yet. This wallet accepts a paymaster only on test networks.

readiness.token-gas.title.en: Paying the network fee in USDC

readiness.token-gas.reason.en: Paying the network fee in USDC runs on the Kernel v3.3 smart account and a token paymaster (Circle’s, or Pimlico’s where Circle has none), and none of them has a published audit for the deployed version. Circle can upgrade or pause its paymaster and change its price source, and Pimlico sets its rate and can decline any operation, so this wallet offers it only on test networks.

readiness.inheritance.reason.en: An heir can sign messages as the account, and so move its tokens through permits, from the moment they are added, not only after the delay, and the owner has no reliable way to notice a takeover attempt in time. It runs on the same unaudited guardian modules, so this wallet offers inheritance only on test networks, as a demonstration.

readiness.dapp-browser.reason.en: The in-app browser runs on a web-view library whose defaults the wallet has to work around, and some gaps (telling which frame of a page sent a request on some Android phones, a page using the camera without asking, downloads that carry the site’s cookies) can be closed only in a real build tested on real phones. Until then it opens only a short fixed list of apps, and only on test networks.

readiness.multisig.reason.en: Multi-signature accounts run on the Kernel v3.3 account with ZeroDev’s weighted signer module as its root, and neither has a published audit for the deployed version. That module accepts a message signature from fewer co-signers than an operation needs, so this wallet never signs messages for these accounts and offers them only on test networks.

readiness.staking.reason.en: Staking hands your ETH to Lido’s or Rocket Pool’s contracts, whose own audits cover the protocols but not how this wallet builds, previews and sends these calls, and that path has not been tested as a real build on real phones. This wallet offers staking only on test networks, where the staked tokens have no value.

readiness.dca.reason.en: A recurring swap gives a key on this phone a Uniswap swap permission whose minimum price is fixed at set-up and does not follow the market, and the account cannot refuse an operation that batches several swaps, so whoever holds the key could sell the account’s ETH at that minimum. It relies on Kernel’s permission modules, which have no published audit, on Uniswap pools whose code is not verified against published source, and on a bundler that asks for an unusually large balance just to estimate the set-up. This wallet offers recurring swaps only on test networks.

readiness.bridge.reason.en: A bridge provider’s contracts and verifiers hold your coins while they move: on the test networks each LayerZero route through Stargate is checked by a single verifier operated by LayerZero Labs, and Stargate’s test pools can be paused by a key whose private part is public. Circle’s USDC transfers would rest on Circle’s own two attesters, and this wallet has not yet sent one. This wallet offers bridging only on test networks, and its bridge path has not been tested as a real build on real phones.

readiness.duress-pin.reason.en: A duress PIN or passphrase opens a separate wallet instead of the real one, so someone looking at the screen sees an ordinary wallet. Anyone who copies this app's files from the phone can tell that two wallets exist, and a 6-digit PIN or a short passphrase can be guessed from such a copy. Funding the second wallet from the real wallet links them on-chain.

readiness.blockers.en: biometric protection of the recovery phrase is opt-in rather than the default, and the wallet has not yet been tested as a real build on real phones

readiness.blockers.protected.en: your recovery phrase is protected by biometrics on this phone, but that protection and the wallet itself have not yet been tested as a real build on real phones

readiness.blockers.unprotected.en: your recovery phrase on this phone is not protected by biometrics (Settings → Recovery phrase protection can turn that on where the phone supports it), and the wallet has not yet been tested as a real build on real phones

readiness.note.enforced.en: Switched off on main networks in this build; it works on the test networks.

readiness.note.advisory.en: Still works on mainnet in this build; not yet cleared for real funds.

settings.hideAmounts.hint.en: Masks every balance and activity amount as •••• (also toggleable with the eye on the Home screen). Addresses stay visible.

settings.autoLock.hint.en: When the app has been in the background at least this long, it locks behind the same biometric prompt as sending. While your recovery phrase (or the active account's imported key) is protected by biometrics, that prompt accepts only biometrics; otherwise your device passcode is offered as a fallback. While auto-lock is on, the wallet also starts locked every time it is opened afresh (after it was closed, swiped away or stopped by the system). Screen state is kept — locking never discards what you were doing.

settings.autoLock.hintWithPin.en: When the app has been in the background at least this long, it locks behind the app PIN pad: it opens again only after you type your 6-digit PIN; the device's own fingerprint, face or passcode prompt does not unlock it while the PIN is on (sending and signing still ask for that prompt). The wallet also starts locked every time it is opened afresh (after it was closed, swiped away or stopped by the system). Screen state is kept — locking never discards what you were doing.

settings.autoLock.withPinNote.en: While the app PIN is on, auto-lock cannot be turned off: the wallet asks for the PIN when it is opened and after this time in the background.

settings.autoLock.unavailable.en: Auto-lock with the device prompt is unavailable on this device: no biometric hardware or enrollment was found, so the unlock prompt could not appear. Set up a device passcode and biometrics to enable it, or turn on the app PIN below (it works without biometrics, but it is weaker than your device's own lock screen, which already protects the secure storage holding your recovery phrase).

settings.aa.simpleNote.en: SimpleAccount (the eth-infinitism v0.7 sample) sends and batches calls, but it has no ERC-1271 support, so it cannot sign messages or logins for dApps.

Paste the KernelFactory address if Kernel v3.3 is deployed on this network; saving checks on-chain, through your RPC endpoint, that the factory, implementation, meta factory and ECDSA validator have code, that the factory uses the pinned implementation, that entrypoint() is v0.7, that accountId() is the expected version, that the meta factory approves the factory and that the validator reports itself as a validator module. Nothing is saved if any check fails.

settings.custom.resetBody.en: The list of networks you added is replaced by an empty one. Tokens, contacts and settings saved for those networks stay on this phone unused and come back if you add the same chain id again. If one of them is active, the wallet switches back to Ethereum mainnet.

settings.networkChip.hint.en: Chooses which network the app's Ethereum account uses

settings.custom.intro.en: Add any EVM network by its chain id and an RPC endpoint. The wallet checks before saving that the endpoint answers as that chain id and that its newest block is recent. A network you add is treated as a MAIN network — its funds may be real — unless you mark it as one of the well-known public test networks. Your addresses are the same on every EVM network.

settings.custom.treatedMain.en: Treated as a MAIN network: its funds may be real. Smart-account features are switched off here.

settings.custom.symbolNote.en: The coin’s symbol is your word: EVM networks do not publish their coin’s symbol on-chain, so the wallet cannot check it and shows it exactly as you type it.

settings.custom.readOnly.en: The saved custom networks could not be read, so nothing was changed. Use “Reset custom networks” in Settings → Developer to start a fresh list.

settings.appLock.offStatus.en: No app PIN or passphrase is set. The wallet unlocks with your fingerprint, face or device passcode.

settings.appLock.backupNote.en: To turn the app PIN or passphrase on, first type two words of your recovery phrase from your written backup, to confirm you still have it.

settings.appLock.strength.en: How hard each is to guess from a copy of this app's files: a 6-digit PIN is one of a million (about 20 bits), which one computer can try in about 3 days. Four random words picked with dice are about 52 bits, millions of years for the same computer. A sentence you make up may be much easier to guess than its length suggests: the 15-character minimum cannot measure that.

settings.appLock.passphraseAdvice.en: A passphrase is typed on your keyboard each time the wallet opens. Use four or more random words, for example picked with dice, not a sentence or quotation someone could guess. Do not use words from your recovery phrase. Do not save it in a password manager: this wallet turns autofill off for it.

settings.appLock.keyboardNote.en: Unlike the PIN pad, your keyboard sees what you type. Use a keyboard you trust.

settings.appLock.sameKind.en: The duress secret is always the same kind as the app lock: a duress PIN with an app PIN, a duress passphrase with an app passphrase.

settings.appLock.noCopy.en: Type the passphrase; do not copy it to the clipboard, where other apps can read it.

settings.duress.funding.en: Fund the second wallet from an exchange or another source that has never sent to or received from this wallet. A transfer between the two wallets links them permanently on the blockchain.

settings.duress.mustDiffer.en: The duress PIN must be different from your app PIN. Nothing was changed.

settings.appLock.notCompleted.en: This could not be completed on this phone. Nothing was changed.

settings.appLock.backupMismatch.en: Those words do not match your recovery phrase. Check your written backup; nothing was changed.

settings.appPin.what.en: With a PIN, the wallet's own lock screen asks for a 6-digit PIN each time the wallet is opened and after auto-lock, instead of your fingerprint or face. The PIN is an extra lock inside this app: your device's own lock still protects the secure storage that holds your recovery phrase, and sending still asks for your fingerprint, face or device passcode.

settings.appPin.limits.en: What the PIN does not protect against: someone who copies this app's storage from the phone can try every 6-digit PIN on a computer, so the PIN stops guessing at the screen only. After 5 wrong PINs the lock screen waits 30 seconds, and the wait doubles with each further wrong PIN up to 1 hour; it never wipes the wallet. There is no PIN reset: if you forget it, clear the app's data or reinstall it, and restore the wallet from your recovery phrase.

settings.appPin.costs.en: While the PIN is on, auto-lock cannot be turned off, screen protection stays on, and the wallet posts no notifications: no reminders for recurring payments or swaps, no price alerts, and no alert when someone starts a recovery or takeover of one of your accounts. You see those the next time you open the wallet.

settings.duress.pin.explanation.en: A duress PIN opens a separate wallet instead of this one, for when someone forces you to open your wallet. Keep a small amount in it and use it now and then so it looks lived in.

settings.duress.pin.claim.en: The duress PIN opens a separate wallet instead of this one, so someone looking at the screen sees an ordinary wallet. Anyone who copies this app's files from the phone can tell that two wallets exist, and a 6-digit PIN can be guessed from such a copy. Funding the second wallet from this wallet links them on-chain.

settings.duress.pin.backup.en: The second wallet is derived from this wallet's recovery phrase (BIP-85, child index 0), so backing up that one phrase backs up both: restoring this phrase and setting a duress PIN again brings the same second wallet back. Its own recovery phrase does not reveal this wallet's: someone shown it learns nothing of this wallet.

settings.duress.pin.needs.en: Turn the app PIN on first: a duress PIN works only on top of it.

settings.appLock.remove.body.en: The wallet will unlock with your fingerprint, face or device passcode again, and notifications can be turned back on.

settings.appPin.remove.withDuress.en: The wallet will unlock with your fingerprint, face or device passcode again. Removing the app PIN also removes the duress PIN and deletes the second wallet from this phone; it can be brought back from this recovery phrase by setting a duress PIN again. Move any funds you want to keep out of the second wallet first.

settings.duress.pin.remove.body.en: The duress PIN stops working and the second wallet is deleted from this phone. It can be brought back from this recovery phrase by setting a duress PIN again. Move any funds you want to keep out of the second wallet first.

settings.appPin.result.on.en: The app PIN is on. The wallet asks for it the next time it is opened or locks.

settings.duress.pin.result.set.en: The duress PIN is set. It opens the second wallet.

settings.duress.pin.result.removed.en: The duress PIN was removed and the second wallet was deleted from this phone.

settings.appPin.result.switched.en: The app lock now uses a 6-digit PIN.

settings.appPassphrase.what.en: With a passphrase, the wallet's own lock screen asks for your passphrase each time the wallet is opened and after auto-lock, instead of your fingerprint or face. The passphrase is an extra lock inside this app: your device's own lock still protects the secure storage that holds your recovery phrase, and sending still asks for your fingerprint, face or device passcode.

settings.appPassphrase.limits.en: What the passphrase does not protect against: someone who copies this app's storage from the phone can try passphrases on a computer. A long, random passphrase makes that impractical; a short or common one does not. After 5 wrong passphrases the lock screen waits 30 seconds, and the wait doubles with each further wrong passphrase up to 1 hour; it never wipes the wallet. There is no passphrase reset: if you forget it, clear the app's data or reinstall it, and restore the wallet from your recovery phrase.

settings.appPassphrase.costs.en: While the app passphrase is on, auto-lock cannot be turned off, screen protection stays on, and the wallet posts no notifications: no reminders for recurring payments or swaps, no price alerts, and no alert when someone starts a recovery or takeover of one of your accounts. You see those the next time you open the wallet.

settings.duress.phr.explanation.en: A duress passphrase opens a separate wallet instead of this one, for when someone forces you to open your wallet. Keep a small amount in it and use it now and then so it looks lived in.

settings.duress.phr.claim.en: The duress passphrase opens a separate wallet instead of this one, so someone looking at the screen sees an ordinary wallet. Anyone who copies this app's files from the phone can tell that two wallets exist and can try to guess both passphrases from such a copy: a long, random passphrase makes that impractical, a short or common one does not. Funding the second wallet from this wallet links them on-chain.

settings.duress.phr.backup.en: The second wallet is derived from this wallet's recovery phrase (BIP-85, child index 0), so backing up that one phrase backs up both: restoring this phrase and setting a duress passphrase again brings the same second wallet back. Its own recovery phrase does not reveal this wallet's: someone shown it learns nothing of this wallet.

settings.duress.phr.needs.en: Turn the app passphrase on first: a duress passphrase works only on top of it.

settings.appPassphrase.remove.withDuress.en: The wallet will unlock with your fingerprint, face or device passcode again. Removing the app passphrase also removes the duress passphrase and deletes the second wallet from this phone; it can be brought back from this recovery phrase by setting a duress passphrase again. Move any funds you want to keep out of the second wallet first.

settings.duress.phr.remove.body.en: The duress passphrase stops working and the second wallet is deleted from this phone. It can be brought back from this recovery phrase by setting a duress passphrase again. Move any funds you want to keep out of the second wallet first.

settings.appPassphrase.result.on.en: The app passphrase is on. The wallet asks for it the next time it is opened or locks.

settings.duress.phr.result.set.en: The duress passphrase is set. It opens the second wallet.

settings.duress.phr.result.removed.en: The duress passphrase was removed and the second wallet was deleted from this phone.

settings.appPassphrase.result.switched.en: The app lock now uses a passphrase.

settings.appLock.pin.notUsable.en: This PIN cannot be used. Choose a different 6-digit PIN.

settings.appLock.pin.mismatch.en: The two PINs you typed are different. Nothing was changed.

settings.appLock.phr.edgeSpace.en: A passphrase cannot begin or end with a space.

settings.appLock.phr.control.en: A passphrase cannot contain line breaks or other control characters.

settings.appLock.phr.invalidText.en: This passphrase contains a character that is not valid text. Type it again.

settings.appLock.phr.notUsable.en: This passphrase cannot be used. Choose a different passphrase.

settings.appLock.phr.phraseWords.en: Do not use words from your recovery phrase in your passphrase.

settings.appLock.phr.mismatch.en: The two passphrases you typed are different. Nothing was changed.

settings.appLock.phraseNotOpened.en: The recovery phrase could not be opened. Nothing was changed.

settings.appLock.phraseNotOpen.en: The recovery phrase is no longer open. Nothing was changed.

settings.reveal.body.en: Make sure no one can see your screen. Anyone who sees these words can steal the funds of every account in this wallet.

settings.wipe.sure.body.en: Without your written recovery phrase, the funds controlled by this wallet will be unrecoverable by anyone, forever.

settings.backup.all.en: One recovery phrase backs up ALL of your accounts — every account in the list above, including hidden ones, on every chain.

settings.backup.keyed.en: One recovery phrase backs up every account in the list above that this wallet holds a key for, including hidden ones, on every chain.

settings.backup.fromPhrase.en: One recovery phrase backs up every account in the list above that comes from it, including hidden ones, on every chain.

settings.backup.watchOnly.en: Watch-only addresses have no key in this wallet, so the recovery phrase does not back them up and is not needed for them: to watch one again on another phone, add its address again.

settings.reveal.warning.en: Never share these words. They control every account in this wallet, not just the active one. Shiba Wallet support will never ask for them. Hide them again as soon as you are done.

settings.reveal.noCopy.en: These words are shown only — there is deliberately no copy button, because anything on the clipboard can be read by other apps. Write them down on paper.

settings.prices.fiatNote.en: Shows an approximate US-dollar value next to balances and on the send and swap confirmation screens. Prices are fetched from CoinGecko (api.coingecko.com), which sees your IP address and which assets are being priced — never your addresses or balances. Turning this off stops all price requests. Prices are indicative only; the exact crypto amount is always the one that counts, and test-network assets are never priced.

settings.prices.keyNote.en: Optional: a free CoinGecko Demo API key (from your CoinGecko developer dashboard) gives a higher rate limit than keyless requests. It is stored only on this device and sent only to api.coingecko.com. Saving runs one live price request with the key first, and nothing is saved if it fails. CoinGecko does not offer a way to confirm a Demo key is genuine, so a pass means the request with the key worked.

settings.endpoints.intro.en: Where balances are fetched from and where transactions are broadcast. Endpoint URLs are public configuration; Dogecoin's Blockbook endpoint may additionally need a provider API key, which is stored only on this device and sent only to that host. Balances refresh with the new endpoint on the next pull-to-refresh. Without a custom endpoint, each chain uses the first of its built-in public defaults that answers; if that one stops answering, the next is tried automatically.

settings.indexer.intro.en: Transaction history on the Activity screen needs an indexer: a standard JSON-RPC endpoint cannot list transactions by address. Paste an endpoint that serves the Transfers API (alchemy_getAssetTransfers). The URL usually contains your own API key — it is stored only on this device and sent only to the endpoint itself. Saving verifies the endpoint first and refuses URLs for the wrong chain.

settings.nftIndexer.intro.en: The NFTs screen needs an indexer that lists the NFTs an address owns (ERC-721 and ERC-1155). Paste the base URL of an endpoint that serves Alchemy's NFT API v3 — it looks like https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/nft/v3/your-key (Sepolia: eth-sepolia). This is a separate URL from the history indexer above, even when both use the same API key. It is stored only on this device and sent only to that host. Saving checks that the indexer answers and that it is indexing this network. NFT images load from the indexer's image cache when possible, otherwise from the NFT's own host or the public ipfs.io gateway, which see your IP address.

settings.aa.mainnetLimit.en: Smart accounts, their modules and gas sponsorship are limited to test networks (see Mainnet readiness above): on a main network these settings cannot be saved and the smart-account options do not appear on the Send, Swap and WalletConnect screens. Clearing a setting saved earlier still works.

settings.aa.intro.en: Optional ERC-4337 setup per EVM chain: a bundler endpoint, a smart-account type (Kernel v3.3 or SimpleAccount) and its factory. Everything is verified before saving — the bundler must answer eth_chainId with this network's chain id and support EntryPoint v0.7, and the factory is checked on-chain through your configured RPC endpoint. When set, the Send and Swap screens offer an experimental "from smart account" toggle (token sends and swaps run as one atomic batch), and WalletConnect can connect dApps to the smart account. Off by default; nothing changes for regular sends.

settings.upgrade.note.en: Turns the active account into a Kernel v3.3 smart account at the same address, on the active network, and shows its current status. You can undo it at any time. The wallet only ever delegates to the pinned Kernel v3.3 contract and never signs an account delegation for a dApp.

settings.sessions.note.en: Let a separate key on this device (or a dApp, over WalletConnect) make only the calls you list, until a deadline you choose. Your Kernel account enforces the limits on-chain, and you can revoke a session at any time. Needs a deployed Kernel v3.3 smart account or an upgraded account. Sessions and their keys are not part of the recovery phrase: they do not survive a wipe or a restore, so revoke them before wiping.

settings.guardians.note.en: Let people you choose replace the key of your deployed Kernel smart account if you lose your recovery phrase. This is a trade-off, not a safety guarantee: enough guardians together could also take the account, and guardians can sign messages as the account from the moment they are installed (with no delay and no veto). Not available for an account upgraded with EIP-7702. The guardian modules have no published audit of their deployed versions.

settings.passkey.needs.en: Needs a deployed Kernel v3.3 smart account (not an EIP-7702 upgrade).

settings.wc.relay.en: Requires a relay project id — create one for free at dashboard.reown.com. The id is public app configuration, not a secret; no account or personal data from this wallet is involved. If a connection was already opened this session, a changed id takes effect after the app restarts.

settings.apps.note.en: A short, fixed list of apps that open inside the wallet, on test networks only. They connect through the same approval sheet as WalletConnect. Their connections are listed on the Connected apps screen (open it with the "Connected apps" button in the WalletConnect section above, or with "Manage connections" in Apps), and a site that is open can be disconnected from the Connection button on its browser bar.

settings.contacts.note.en: Named addresses for each chain, picked from the Send screen. A name is shown only for an exact address match, always with the full address; look-alike addresses get a warning instead.

settings.proof.note.en: Sign a challenge you were given (or your own statement) with this account or its smart account, and share a proof anyone can check. Website logins are not signed here — they go through WalletConnect.

settings.tokens.track.en: Track ERC-20 tokens on the Home screen: balances, and sending them.

settings.approvals.note.en: See which contracts may move your tracked tokens and NFT collections without asking you again, and revoke them. Revoking is an ordinary transaction with a normal network fee.

settings.swaps.note.en: Swapping (the Swap link on the Home screen) is priced by the 0x aggregator and needs your own API key — create one for free at dashboard.0x.org. The key is stored only on this device and sent only to api.0x.org with quote requests; it is never bundled or committed anywhere. Saving verifies the key first with one live quote request (nothing is traded), and a rejected key is not saved. The feature stays off until a key is saved here.

settings.swaps.noAddress.en: No Ethereum address is available to verify the key with.

settings.danger.note.en: Wiping removes the recovery phrase from this device's secure storage. Your written backup remains the only way to restore the wallet.

settings.about.en: Shiba Wallet is non-custodial: keys are generated, stored and used only on this device.

settings.insecureEndpoint.en: Endpoints must use https:// (plain http:// is accepted only for localhost or 10.0.2.2 during development).

settings.passkey.explanation.en: A passkey becomes an ADDITIONAL signer on your smart account, protected by this phone’s biometrics. Your recovery phrase stays in control: it can remove the passkey at any time, and your smart-account address does not change. One passkey per account.

settings.passkey.risk.en: Risk: anyone who can use this passkey can spend from the smart account. The account contract would also let the passkey change the account’s own settings — even replace your recovery phrase as the owner. This wallet refuses to let the passkey do that, but the refusal is in this app, not enforced on-chain. Protect the passkey like your recovery phrase.

settings.passkey.audit.en: The WebAuthn validator version this wallet uses (ZeroDev WebAuthnValidator v0.0.3) has no published audit; the audited version had a flaw that this version fixes. Treat passkeys as experimental with real funds.

settings.multisig.listHint.en: Multi-signature accounts have no key of their own: this wallet holds one of their signers, a recovery-phrase account, and every operation also needs the co-signers. On another phone, add one again from its record on the Multisig screen.

settings.multisig.blurb.en: Accounts that need several signers for every operation: this wallet’s account plus co-signers on other phones. Transactions only: a multi-signature account never signs messages, logins or token permits. Test networks only; the signer module has no published audit.

settings.spending.hint.en: Set a maximum per token over a time window (for example 0.1 ETH per 24 hours) for this account on this network. The app checks it before it signs a send, swap, smart-account operation or WalletConnect transaction.

settings.spending.honesty.en: Enforced by this app only. Anyone with your recovery phrase, and keys used outside this app, are not limited.

settings.dev.minFee.switch.en: Send the next regular-account transaction at the minimum fee (to rehearse Speed up / Cancel)

settings.dev.minFee.hint.en: Test networks only. The next native-coin or token send from the Send screen, with the smart account off, is priced at a max fee of 1 wei and a priority fee of 1 wei per gas. A block can include a transaction only if its max fee is at least the block’s base fee, so while the base fee is above 1 wei this one stays in the network’s pool until you speed it up or cancel it from Activity; the speed-up or cancellation is priced at the node’s normal fee suggestion, so a block can include it. The option turns itself off once that transaction is sent; going back from the confirm screen leaves it on, and it is off again whenever the app restarts. NFT sends, swaps, staking, app requests and smart-account operations are always priced normally. The node may refuse such an under-priced transaction outright ("transaction underpriced"); that is expected, because the nodes behind one endpoint address can apply different minimums, and the option then stays on until a send goes through or you turn it off. On the layer-2 test networks the transaction goes to the network’s sequencer, which may refuse it rather than hold it; that has not been tried.

settings.protect.message.en: After this, opening your recovery phrase needs your fingerprint or face. If you ever add or remove a fingerprint or face, or turn off the screen lock, this phone will no longer be able to open the phrase and you will need your written backup. Make sure your written recovery phrase is safe before continuing.

settings.protect.cancelled.en: Moving your phrase to biometric protection was cancelled.

settings.protect.notAttempted.en: Your recovery phrase is in standard secure storage. You can move it into biometric-protected storage below.

settings.protect.noStrongBiometrics.en: This phone has no strong fingerprint or face unlock enrolled, so the phrase is in standard secure storage: code inside the app can read it while the phone is unlocked, and your screen lock is the main protection.

settings.protect.policyOff.en: Biometric protection is turned off for this build.

settings.protect.reverted.en: The protected copy stopped working after a biometric change; the wallet is using its standard copy.

settings.protect.standardCopy.en: An unprotected copy is still being removed; it goes the next time you approve something.

settings.wc.status.saved.en: Saved — used to reach the WalletConnect relay.

settings.wc.status.builtIn.en: Built-in project id — used to reach the WalletConnect relay. You can replace it with your own.

settings.wc.clear.a11y.en: Use the built-in WalletConnect project id instead of the saved one

settings.wc.clear.message.en: The project id you saved is removed from this phone, and the wallet's built-in project id is used again to reach the WalletConnect relay. If a connection was already opened this session, the change takes effect after the app restarts.

settings.notifications.switch.en: Remind me when something is due

settings.notifications.what.en: When this is on, this phone shows a reminder when one of your recurring payments falls due or one of your recurring swaps does, a notice when a price alert on your watchlist is reached, and an alert when the takeover check on the Inheritance screen finds that a recovery of one of your accounts was started. A reminder never sends anything: each payment or swap is still sent only after you confirm it in the wallet, and a price alert never buys, sells or sends.

settings.notifications.privacy.en: The reminders are scheduled on this phone by the wallet itself. No notification service is used and nothing about them leaves the device. They say only what kind of event happened, never an amount, an address or a name, because notifications can appear on the lock screen.

settings.notifications.limits.en: Reminders are worked out from what the wallet read the last time it was open, so a change made elsewhere is picked up the next time you open it. After a force stop, Android drops the scheduled reminders until you open the wallet again. Not included: merchant subscriptions (the merchant collects those payments, not this wallet) and auto-lock reminders.

settings.notifications.statusOff.en: Reminders are off. Nothing is scheduled.

settings.notifications.denied.en: Notifications are turned off for Shiba Wallet in this phone’s settings, so no reminder can be shown. Allow notifications for Shiba Wallet in the system settings, then turn this on again.

accounts.paste.unreadable.en: The clipboard could not be read. Type the address instead.

accounts.hide.body.en: Hiding only removes it from the lists. Its addresses, funds and keys are unchanged, it stays recoverable from your recovery phrase, and you can show it again here at any time.

accounts.keyNotOpened.en: The key could not be opened.

accounts.row.importedNote.en: imported private key, Ethereum only — NOT backed up by your recovery phrase

accounts.derivationNote.en: Account addresses from the phrase follow the common conventions: Ethereum m/44'/60'/0'/0/N (as MetaMask), Solana m/44'/501'/N'/0' (as Phantom), Bitcoin m/84'/0'/N'/0/0 and Dogecoin m/44'/3'/N'/0/0. After restoring the phrase on a new device, add accounts again in the same order to get the same addresses back.

accounts.importKey.hint.en: Adds an account from a single Ethereum private key. It is not backed up by your recovery phrase.

accounts.watch.buttonHint.en: Follows an Ethereum address without its key. The wallet cannot sign for it; a send for it can be prepared for an off-line signer.

accounts.watch.intro.en: Follow any Ethereum address without its key: its balances, tokens, activity and NFTs appear like an account’s, but the wallet cannot sign, swap or recover anything for it. A send on an Ethereum network can still be prepared here and signed by an off-line signer that holds its key.

accounts.watch.privacy.en: Watching an address reveals your interest in it to the network endpoints and indexers this wallet uses (Settings → Network endpoints and the history and NFT indexers), because the wallet asks them about this address.

accounts.watchOnly.rowNote.en: watch-only, no key in this wallet — it cannot sign; a send can be prepared for an off-line signer

accounts.watchOnly.listHint.en: Watch-only accounts are addresses this wallet follows without a key; your recovery phrase has nothing to back up for them.

accounts.removeImported.confirmMessage.en: Only continue if you have the private key written down or stored elsewhere, or the account is empty.

accounts.revealImported.message.en: Make sure no one can see your screen. Anyone who sees this key controls the account. Keeping a copy of it is the only backup this account has.

accounts.multisig.listHint.en: Listed here for reference only. They are managed on the Multisig screen (Settings → Multi-signature accounts) and cannot be hidden here.

recordsBackup.what.en: A records backup is one file with the records this wallet keeps on this phone: contacts, transaction notes, networks you added, tracked tokens, guardian recovery records, multi-signature account records, bridge transfers, price alerts and spending limits. It contains no private key, no recovery phrase and no PIN.

recordsBackup.key.en: The file is encrypted with a key made from this wallet’s recovery phrase, so only this recovery phrase can open it — on this phone, or on another phone after you restore the phrase there. If you lose the recovery phrase, this backup is lost with it.

recordsBackup.notIncluded.en: Not in the backup and not restored by it: session keys (they never leave this phone; a payment, subscription or recurring swap must be revoked and set up again), imported private keys (only the copy of the key you kept yourself can restore such an account) and passkeys (the phone’s passkey provider holds them, not this wallet). Account names, watched addresses, connected apps, pending transactions and spending history are not included either.

recordsBackup.merge.en: Restoring adds only the records that are not on this phone yet. A record that is already here — the same contact address, note, network, token, account, transfer, alert or limit — is kept exactly as it is and never overwritten. Each record is checked as when it was first saved, and a network you added is checked again through its RPC address. A multi-signature account comes back without its operation history.

recordsBackup.file.en: The file is shared through the share sheet (for example to your cloud drive). The temporary copy on this phone is deleted a minute after the share sheet closes.

sessions.handover.title.en: Delete the key from this device?

sessions.handover.body.en: Only do this once the merchant has the key. It cannot be shown again; if it was lost, revoke the subscription and create a new one.

sessions.forget.body.en: It is removed from this list (and its key from this device).

sessions.reset.body.en: The unreadable list is cleared. This does NOT revoke anything on-chain: grants stay active until they expire, and the session keys the old list referenced stay unused in secure storage.

sessions.signed.sessionKey.en: Signed by the session key only.

sessions.signed.recurring.en: Signed by this recurring payment’s own key only, not by your account key.

sessions.signed.dca.en: Signed by this recurring swap’s own key only, not by your account key.

sessions.notIncluded.en: Not included within two minutes. It may still be included; the list reads the status from the chain.

sessions.install.signed.en: Signed by your account key as the account's root validator.

sessions.install.estimatePassed.en: Bundler gas estimate passed (eth_estimateUserOperationGas simulated the install).

sessions.handover.button.en: Hand the key to the merchant

sessions.handover.done.en: The merchant has the key — delete it here

sessions.handover.notNow.en: Not now (keep it on this device)

sessions.requote.en: Starting the clock now and asking the bundler again…

sessions.subscription.intro.en: Lets one merchant take up to a fixed amount once per period, until the payments run out or you revoke. A new key is created for the merchant; your account enforces the limits on-chain.

sessions.reading.en: Reading the account and asking the bundler…

sessions.revoke.call.en: One call to your own account: uninstallValidation for this permission

sessions.grant.intro.en: A session key is a new key on this device that may make ONLY the calls you list, until it expires. Your account enforces the limits on-chain. Each value cap is per call, not a total.

sessions.noAddress.en: No Ethereum address for this account.

sessions.list.unreadable.en: The saved session list could not be read. Nothing was changed. Grants on-chain are not affected.

sessions.list.partial.en: Some saved sessions could not be read and are not shown.

sessions.payNow.hint.en: Checks the payment with the network, then asks you to confirm before anything is sent.

sessions.handover.once.en: Hand the key to the merchant (shown once)

sessions.audit.en: The session permission modules (ZeroDev ECDSASigner, CallPolicy v0.0.4, TimestampPolicy, GasPolicy) have no published security audit that names them. Treat sessions as experimental with real funds.

sessions.wipeWarning.en: Sessions are enforced by your account on-chain, but this list and the session keys exist only on this device. Wiping the wallet or restoring it from the recovery phrase loses both, while the grants stay active on-chain until they expire. Revoke sessions you no longer need before wiping, and revoke everything you no longer recognise.

sessions.installMode.en: Installed with an ordinary operation signed by your account key, so the permission is live on-chain before the session key signs anything. (The alternative "enable mode" signature is not used: an unused enable signature cannot be cancelled before it expires.)

sessions.subscription.keyWarning.en: This is the subscription key. Whoever holds it can take payments from your account within the limits above until you revoke or it expires. Give it only to the merchant, over a channel you trust. It is shown once: after you confirm the hand-over it is deleted from this device.

sessions.subscription.expiredUnhanded.en: This subscription expired before its key was handed to the merchant, so there is nothing left to hand over: no payment can be taken any more. Revoke it to remove the permission from your account (the key is deleted from this device too), then Forget it.

sessions.recurring.cardNote.en: Sent only while this wallet is open, and only after you confirm each payment; no payment is ever sent in the background. With reminders on (Settings → Privacy → Notifications), this phone can remind you when a payment falls due, even while the wallet is closed; the payment still waits for you.

sessions.recurring.completed.en: No more payments can be sent. Revoke it to remove the permission from your account (the payment key is deleted from this phone too); it is then forgotten here.

sessions.recurring.intro.en: Pays one recipient up to a fixed amount once per period from your smart account, until the payments run out or you revoke. A new payment key is created on this phone and never leaves it; your account enforces the limits on-chain.

sessions.recurring.reminders.en: Reminders: with "Remind me when something is due" on (Settings → Privacy → Notifications), this phone shows a reminder when a payment falls due, even while the wallet is closed. Reminders need the wallet’s own build of the app; they do not work inside Expo Go. A reminder never sends anything: sending while the wallet is closed would need a decision on whether a payment may ever go out without you confirming it, so this version always asks you first.

sessions.recurring.payPrompt.en: You confirm each payment in the wallet. The payment key signs it, not your account key, so your recovery phrase is never opened for it. If the payment key is protected by biometrics (it is when your recovery phrase was protected at set-up), the phone also asks once: "Use the session key".

sessions.recurring.spending.en: Your spending limits (this app only) are checked before each payment, by the payment amount: a payment that would go over a limit is not sent. The network fee of a recurring payment is not counted against limits; the fee budget caps it on-chain.

sessions.recurring.whileOpen.en: Payments are sent only while this wallet is open. When one is due, the wallet shows it on this screen (and in a banner when you open the app) and sends it only after you confirm. Nothing is sent in the background or while the wallet is closed. A payment missed while the wallet was closed is not lost: your account allows it to be sent later, until the end date.

sessions.dca.reservation.en: A recurring swap’s set-up is unusually large (about 7 million gas), and the bundler asks the smart account to hold its worst-case fee before it will estimate it — about 0.012 ETH on 2026-10-11, more when fees are higher. Fund the smart account, then review again.

dca.floorNote.en: The minimum is fixed when you start and never follows the price afterwards. Review reads a fresh quote and computes the minimum from it at this percentage.

dca.reading.en: Reading the pool, the account and asking the bundler…

dca.estimatePassed.en: Bundler gas estimate passed (eth_estimateUserOperationGas simulated the set-up).

dca.swapNow.hint.en: Checks the swap with the network and reads a fresh quote, then asks you to confirm before anything is sent.

dca.cardNote.en: Sent only while this wallet is open, and only after you confirm each swap; no swap is ever sent in the background. With reminders on (Settings → Privacy → Notifications), this phone can remind you when a swap falls due, even while the wallet is closed; the swap still waits for you.

dca.completed.en: No more swaps can be sent. Revoke it to remove the permission from your account (the swap key is deleted from this phone too); it is then forgotten here.

subscriptionKey.fileNote.en: Sends the key as a .json file through the share sheet. Choose a channel you trust; the temporary copy on this phone is deleted a few seconds after the share sheet closes.

swap.off.en: Swapping trades one asset for another directly from this wallet, priced by the 0x aggregator. It is off because no 0x API key is configured. Create a free key at dashboard.0x.org, then save it under Settings → Swaps — saving verifies the key with one live quote request. The key is stored only on this device and sent only to api.0x.org.

swap.sessionExpired.en: Smart-account session expired; go back and quote again.

swap.aa.reverted.en: The bundler reports the operation was included but reverted on-chain: none of the batch took effect, and the gas was still charged to the smart account.

swap.aa.single.en: One operation with a single call: the swap (selling the native coin needs no approval).

swap.minimumEnforced.en: The guaranteed minimum is enforced by the swap transaction itself: if the market moves past your slippage setting, the transaction fails instead of filling for less.

swap.noGasEstimate.en: The quote carried no gas estimate; the exact fee is shown at the confirm step.

swap.checkingAllowance.en: Checking allowance and preparing the transaction…

swap.ownFee.en: Our own worst-case fee — priced exactly like a regular send — is shown on the confirm screen before anything is signed.

swap.unavailable.en: Swapping unavailable — no configured Ethereum endpoint.

swap.balance.failed.en: could not be loaded right now.

swap.quotesNote.en: Quotes come from the 0x aggregator using your API key (Settings → Swaps). Nothing is signed or sent until you confirm on the next screens; a quote older than a minute is refreshed before anything executes.

staking.approving.en: Approving, then waiting for the approval to take effect…

staking.intro.en: Staking puts test ETH into a liquid-staking protocol and gives you a token for it. These are test networks: the tokens have no value.

staking.unreadable.en: The staking contracts could not be read right now.

staking.claim.note.en: Claims every finalized Lido withdrawal request of this account.

staking.reading.en: Reading the protocol and preparing the quote…

staking.source.hint.en: Opens the source in the browser

staking.simulation.unavailable.en: The outcome simulation is not available from this endpoint right now.

broadcast.unknown.title.en: No answer from the network in time.

broadcast.handedOver.title.en: Already handed to the network once.

broadcast.handedOver.en: This transaction was already handed to the network endpoint once and whether it was accepted is still unknown, so this wallet did not hand it over a second time. Check Pending on this phone in Activity; review a new send only if that list says it was dropped.

coldAa.switch.hint.en: Sends from the watched address’s own Kernel v3.3 smart account instead; the off-line signer signs the operation as its owner

coldAa.accountNote.en: The smart account is the watched address’s Kernel v3.3 account at CREATE2 index 0, the address that follows from the owner alone. The off-line signer holds the owner key and signs the operation; the smart account pays its own network fee from its balance and EntryPoint deposit (no paymaster, no fee in a token).

coldAa.paymasterNotUsed.en: The sponsorship paymaster saved for this network is not used here: with an off-line signer the smart account pays its own network fee.

coldAa.qrContents.en: These QR codes contain only the unsigned smart-account operation (the network, the EntryPoint, the smart account, its owner, the nonce, the gas limits, the fees and the calls), a plain summary, the userOpHash, the digest to sign and a request number. They contain no key and no secret: anyone who sees them learns what you plan to send, but cannot send it.

coldAa.checkOnSigner.en: Before signing, check on the off-line signer that it decodes the same recipient, amount, network, smart account and worst-case fee as this screen. Sign only if they match.

coldAa.formatNote.en: This is Shiba Wallet’s own request format (shiba-wallet/cold-sign-userop-request, version 1), not the EIP-4527 format some hardware signers read, so the off-line signer must understand this format.

coldAa.feesFixed.en: The network fees are fixed now: the owner’s signature covers them, so they cannot be raised after signing. If the bundler’s minimum fee rises above them before you submit, the wallet refuses to submit, and you review the send again and have a new request signed.

coldAa.scanNote.en: Scan the signature the off-line signer shows. A signature for a different request, from a key other than the owner’s or over a changed operation is refused. The wallet submits to the bundler only after it has checked that the owner signed exactly the operation shown above.

coldAa.reviewAgain.en: The request is kept only while this screen is open, and only until it expires. If you leave, review the send again and have the new request signed; an old signature is refused for a new request.

coldAa.scanRationale.en: The camera reads the signature QR code the off-line signer shows. Nothing is sent until the wallet has checked it.

home.delegation.warningHint.en: Opens the account upgrade screen to review this

home.delegation.foreign.en: This is not the wallet's Kernel delegate. If you did not do this, revoke it now.

bridge.reset.body.en: This forgets every bridge transfer listed on this phone. Nothing on the network changes.

bridge.noBundlerForReceipt.en: No bundler is configured for that network any more, so the smart-account operation’s receipt cannot be read.

bridge.amountZero.en: Enter an amount greater than zero.

bridge.chooseNetwork.en: Choose the network to send to.

bridge.smartUnreadable.en: The smart account could not be read just now; go back and try again.

bridge.noProviderForPair.en: No provider can be chosen for this pair of networks.

bridge.approval.confirmed.en: Approval confirmed. The burn was quoted after the approval; these are its final numbers.

bridge.success.noReceipt.en: No receipt yet. The operation may still be included — keep the UserOperation hash above to look it up later. The transfer below can be followed once the bundle transaction is known.

bridge.success.reverted.en: The bundler reports the operation was included but reverted on-chain. The gas was still charged to the smart account. Nothing was bridged.

bridge.confirm.pinnedTitle.en: Written into the call and checked by this wallet

bridge.approve.title.en: Step 1 of 2 — Approve exactly the amount

bridge.form.reading.en: Reading the provider’s contracts and preparing the quote…

bridge.record.mintSent.en: Mint transaction sent from this wallet

bridge.record.deliverySent.en: Delivery transaction sent from this wallet

bridge.intro.en: Bridging moves test ETH or USDC from this network to another test network. A bridge provider carries the transfer, and you trust the provider’s contracts and verifiers while it is on its way, so each provider below says who that is. These are test networks: the coins have no value.

bridge.choiceNote.en: You choose the provider. The wallet lists every provider it knows for this asset and this pair of networks and never picks one for you.

bridge.amount.usdcHint.en: USDC has 6 decimal places; an amount with more is refused, not rounded.

bridge.timeNotPromise.en: A time measured once is not a promise: delivery waits for the verifiers and the executor, and either can take longer.

bridge.feeBeforeQuote.en: Fee: quoted live from the provider’s contracts when you tap Get quotes or Review.

bridge.singleProvider.en: One provider serves this route; choose it to continue.

bridge.records.note.en: Transfers sent from this screen are kept on this phone (the newest 64) and followed here whenever this screen is open. The sending transaction also appears in Activity.

bridge.records.readOnly.en: The list of bridge transfers on this phone could not be read in full, so it is not changed: transfers sent now are followed only until the app is closed. Reset the transfer list to start a new one; nothing on the network changes.

bridge.refusal.listingOnly.en: This provider was built for listing only; nothing can be quoted with it.

bridge.refusal.ethereumOnly.en: Bridging works only on Ethereum networks.

bridge.offer.chooseUsdc.en: Choose USDC above to bridge USDC with Circle CCTP.

bridge.providerComing.en: Listed for comparison; not offered for sending in this version.

bridge.logTooOld.en: This transfer was sent too long ago for the wallet to search the receiving network for it; look up the sending transaction in LayerZero Scan or an explorer.

bridge.logTooOldCctp.en: This transfer was sent too long ago for the wallet to search the receiving network for its mint; look up the recipient on that network in an explorer. If the USDC was never minted, anyone can still send the mint with Circle’s attested message.

bridge.refusal.nativeSmart.en: Test ETH is bridged only to your regular account: Stargate hands ETH over with a 2,300-gas transfer, which a deployed smart account cannot accept. Nothing was quoted.

bridge.refusal.notOffered.en: This bridge provider is not offered in this wallet.

bridge.refusal.builtInOnly.en: Bridging is offered only to the built-in test networks.

bridge.refusal.otherAccount.en: This quote was prepared for another account. Nothing was quoted.

bridge.refusal.value.en: The transaction would not carry the quoted value. Nothing was signed.

bridge.refusal.noApproval.en: This transfer needs no token approval.

bridge.refusal.approvalMismatch.en: The approval transaction would not be the exact approval quoted. Nothing was signed.

bridge.refusal.regularOnly.en: This quote was prepared for the regular account. Nothing was quoted.

bridge.refusal.aaNetwork.en: The smart-account setup is for another network than this quote. Nothing was quoted.

bridge.refusal.calls.en: The operation would not carry the quoted calls and value. Nothing was signed.

bridge.refusal.aaAddress.en: This quote was read for another address than the smart account. Nothing was quoted.

bridge.lz.pin.noOptions.en: No extra options and no compose message: the transfer cannot run code of its own on the receiving network.

bridge.cctp.firstMintPaymaster.en: Circle's USDC fee paymaster cannot pay for the first mint on a network where this account holds no USDC: it takes its fee before the mint runs.

bridge.cctp.call.oneOperation.en: One smart-account operation carries both calls, all or nothing, so there is one device prompt.

bridge.cctp.call.twoTransactions.en: Two transactions, each with its own device prompt: first the approval, then, once it is confirmed, the burn.

bridge.cctp.pin.caller.en: Destination caller: none (zero), so anyone may send the mint; it still goes only to the recipient above.

bridge.cctp.pin.standard.en: Maximum fee 0 and finality 2000: a Standard Transfer, which Circle attests after the sending network’s hard finality. This wallet never builds a Fast Transfer.

bridge.userop.waiting.en: Waiting for the bundle transaction that carries the smart-account operation; tracking starts once it is known.

bridge.userop.notIncluded.en: The smart-account operation has not been included yet: the bundler has no receipt for it. Tracking starts once it is included in a bundle transaction.

bridge.userop.reverted.en: The smart-account operation was included but reverted, so nothing was bridged; its network fee was still charged.

bridge.userop.malformed.en: The bundler’s receipt for the smart-account operation was not in the expected shape, so the wallet did not use it and will ask again.

bridge.status.notAsked.en: The wallet has not asked where this transfer is yet.

bridge.cctp.expiry.unknown.en: Circle’s attested message is valid until it is used, unless it carries an expiration block: Circle’s technical guide says an expired message must be re-attested by Circle (possible at any time) before it can be minted.

bridge.cctp.expiry.none.en: The attested message carries no expiration block (0), so it stays valid until the mint is sent: Circle’s contract accepts such a message at any time, and only once.

bridge.cctp.expiry.arbitrum.en: (on Arbitrum an Ethereum block number, as Circle’s guide notes)

bridge.refusal.noMint.en: There is no mint transaction to send for this transfer.

bridge.refusal.noDelivery.en: There is no delivery transaction to send for this transfer.

multisig.noEndpoint.en: No RPC endpoint is configured for this network.

multisig.chooseToken.en: Choose a token tracked on this network.

multisig.noBundler.en: No bundler is configured for this network (Settings → Account Abstraction).

multisig.cosigner.scanRationale.en: Scan the co-signer’s Ethereum address QR code.

multisig.create.threshold.en: Threshold: the combined weight every operation needs (at least two signers).

multisig.detail.qrCaption.en: The multisig account’s address. Anyone can send to it; moving funds out needs the co-signers.

multisig.detail.newOperation.body.en: The one you are collecting approvals for will be discarded.

multisig.detail.shareTitle.en: Share the account with the co-signers

multisig.detail.shareHint.en: A co-signer adds the same account on their phone from this record (it contains no secrets).

multisig.send.intro.en: This builds a signing request for the co-signers; nothing is signed or sent until enough of them approve and you submit.

multisig.collect.step1.en: 1. Send this request to the co-signers

multisig.collect.paste.en: Paste a co-signer’s approval (or a 65-byte signature from another wallet)

multisig.collect.addFile.en: Add an approval from a file

multisig.confirm.fee.en: Network fee (worst case, set by you as the submitter)

multisig.confirm.ownBalance.en: Paid from the multisig’s own balance.

multisig.confirm.deploys.en: This operation also deploys the multisig account (its first operation).

multisig.progress.timeoutHint.en: The bundler has not reported it within two minutes. It may still be included; the UserOperation hash is the lookup key.

multisig.import.title.en: Add a multisig from its record

multisig.import.intro.en: Scan the account record on another signer’s phone, paste the text they shared, or open its file. The wallet checks that the address follows from the signer set and that one of your recovery-phrase accounts is a signer.

multisig.cosign.intro.en: Scan the signing request on the submitter’s phone (a long request comes in several QR codes; scan each one), paste the text they shared, or open its file. You will see the account, the network, the nonce and every call in full before anything is signed.

multisig.cosign.doneTitle.en: Approval ready — give it to the submitter

multisig.list.intro.en: An account that needs several signers for every operation: this wallet’s account plus co-signers on other phones, each with a weight, and a threshold.

multisig.list.cosignedElsewhere.en: Approved as a co-signer (accounts not in this wallet)

multisig.list.add.en: Add a multisig from a record

multisig.unverifiedNetwork.en: Multi-signature accounts need the Kernel v3.3 contracts and ZeroDev's weighted signer module on this network; the wallet has not verified them here.

multisig.refused.title.en: Not available for a multi-signature account

multisig.file.unavailable.en: Sharing files is not available on this device. Use Share… or Copy instead.

multisig.file.hint.en: Shares the text as a .json file (for example to a messaging app or your cloud drive). It contains no secrets; the temporary copy on this phone is deleted a minute after the share sheet closes.

multisig.freshDeploy.en: A multi-signature account is always a new account, deployed fresh with its signer set. This wallet never converts an existing account: Kernel keeps the old single-key validator installed when the root signer changes, so a converted account would still obey one key, a backdoor around the co-signers.

multisig.feesLine.en: Co-signers approve the calls and the nonce, not the network fee or paymaster, which the submitter sets.

multisig.unaudited.en: The weighted signer module and the Kernel v3.3 account it runs on have no published audit for their deployed versions, so this wallet offers multi-signature accounts on test networks only.

multisig.deployNote.en: Not deployed yet. The first operation deploys the account; it needs the co-signers’ approvals like every operation, and the account pays the network fee from its own balance, so fund the address first.

multisig.fundAndRetry.en: The co-signer approvals stay valid while you fund the multisig, as long as no other operation uses this nonce: fund it, then review and submit again without collecting them again.

multisig.phraseSignerOnly.en: A multi-signature account is created with this wallet’s active recovery-phrase account as one of its signers. Switch to an account from your recovery phrase first (imported keys and watch-only addresses cannot be the wallet’s signer).

multisig.config.singleSigner.en: With these weights and this threshold one signer alone could send operations, which is not a multi-signature account. Raise the threshold or lower the heaviest weight so every operation needs at least two signers.

multisig.approval.submitter.en: This approval is from this wallet’s own signer, which submits the operation and signs it last. The signer module counts each signer once, so it cannot also be a co-signer approval.

multisig.exposure.alwaysLocal.en: , so this phone’s signer is always one of them

multisig.refused.guardians.en: Guardians are not available for a multi-signature account: its root signer module is the same contract guardian recovery uses, and the account keys a module by its address, so the signer set and a guardian set would collide on one validation id and one storage slot.

multisig.refused.inheritance.en: Inheritance is not available for a multi-signature account: it is built on the guardian module, which is the same contract as the account’s root signer module, so the two would collide.

multisig.refused.passkeys.en: A passkey signer is not offered for a multi-signature account: it would let one passkey act for the account without the co-signers, and adding one to a multisig root has never been tested.

multisig.refused.sessionKeys.en: Session keys are not offered for a multi-signature account: a session key would let one key act for the account without the co-signers, and adding one to a multisig root has never been tested.

multisig.refused.eip7702.en: An EIP-7702 upgrade is not applicable: it upgrades a regular account’s own address, and a multi-signature account is already a deployed smart account with no single owner key.

multisig.refused.ownerRotation.en: A multi-signature account has no single owner key to change; its signer set is fixed when it is deployed.

multisig.config.threshold.en: The threshold must be a whole number of at least 1.

multisig.storeDamaged.en: The list of multi-signature accounts on this phone could not be read, so nothing was changed. The accounts themselves are on-chain; import their records again if the list stays unreadable.

multisig.remove.title.en: Remove this multisig from this wallet?

multisig.import.noRecord.en: No multisig record found in the text.

multisig.import.invalidJson.en: The multisig record is not valid JSON.

multisig.import.isRequest.en: This is a signing request, not an account record. Open it under “Approve a request”.

multisig.import.isApproval.en: This is a co-signer’s approval, not an account record.

multisig.import.notRecord.en: This is not a Shiba Wallet multisig record.

multisig.import.detailsMissing.en: The multisig account details are missing.

multisig.import.badChainId.en: The multisig record has no valid chain id.

multisig.import.badAccount.en: The multisig record has no valid account address.

multisig.import.noSigners.en: The multisig record lists no signers.

multisig.import.badThreshold.en: The multisig record has no valid threshold.

multisig.import.delay.en: This wallet supports multisig accounts without a delay only.

multisig.import.badIndex.en: The multisig record has no valid index.

multisig.import.otherDeployment.en: This multisig uses deployment addresses this wallet does not use (factory, implementation or signer module).

multisig.import.noOwnSigner.en: None of this wallet’s recovery-phrase accounts is a signer of this multisig, so it cannot approve or submit for it. Add the account that is a signer first, or watch the address instead (Settings → Accounts).

multisig.noSlot.en: No multisig slot is left in this wallet.

multisig.create.noDelay.en: This wallet creates multisig accounts without a delay.

multisig.create.mustBeSigner.en: This wallet’s signer must be one of the multisig’s signers.

multisig.create.tooMany.en: This phone already holds too many multisig accounts with this exact signer set on this network.

multisig.notInWallet.en: This multisig is not in this wallet.

multisig.notInWalletAnyMore.en: This multisig is not in this wallet any more.

multisig.chain.match.en: Deployed; its signer set and threshold on-chain match this record.

multisig.chain.notVisible.en: Deployed by its first operation (the bundler’s receipt confirmed it), but the network endpoint does not show the account’s code yet, so its signer set could not be compared on-chain. Open the multisig again in a moment.

multisig.depositNote.en: The EntryPoint holds this deposit for the multisig and takes network fees from it first. It cannot be sent as an amount, and this wallet does not offer a way to withdraw it; later operations use it for their fees.

multisig.funding.recordedDeploy.en: For scale only: in this wallet’s recorded test run on Ethereum Sepolia (2026-10-10), the first operation of a 2-of-3 multisig, which also deployed it, was quoted at a worst-case network fee of about 0.0036 to 0.0066 test ETH at different fee levels and actually cost about 0.0020 test ETH. That is a recorded range, not a quote for this operation; fees change.

multisig.funding.recordedLater.en: For scale only: in this wallet’s recorded test run on Ethereum Sepolia (2026-10-10), a later operation of a 2-of-3 multisig was quoted at a worst-case network fee of about 0.0013 to 0.0023 test ETH at different fee levels and actually cost about 0.0008 test ETH. That is a recorded range, not a quote for this operation; fees change.

multisig.funding.balanceUnread.en: Its balance could not be read just now.

multisig.funding.unknown.en: The exact amount is unknown because the estimate itself was refused.

multisig.preview.note.en: Simulated as direct calls from the multisig account. The network fee the multisig pays through the EntryPoint is shown separately above and is not part of this list.

multisig.preview.undeployed.en: The multisig is not deployed yet: this operation deploys it first, which the simulation leaves out (deploying it moves no funds apart from the network fee).

multisig.submit.notCollecting.en: This operation was already submitted or replaced. Nothing was signed.

multisig.submit.callsDiffer.en: The quoted calls differ from the ones the co-signers approved. Nothing was signed.

multisig.submit.noCalls.en: Nothing to send: the operation has no calls.

multisig.request.notFound.en: No multisig signing request found in the text.

multisig.request.invalidJson.en: The signing request is not valid JSON.

multisig.request.isApproval.en: This is a co-signer’s approval, not a signing request. Add it on the submitting phone.

multisig.request.isRecord.en: This is an account record, not a signing request.

multisig.request.notRequest.en: This is not a Shiba Wallet multisig signing request.

multisig.request.otherNetwork.en: The request and its account are on different networks.

multisig.request.otherAccount.en: The request is for a different account than its account details.

multisig.request.otherModule.en: The request names a different signer module than its account.

multisig.request.badCall.en: A call in the request is malformed.

multisig.request.callsMismatch.en: The listed calls do not match the request’s call data. Nothing can be approved.

multisig.cosign.noSigner.en: None of this wallet’s accounts is a signer of this multisig, so there is nothing to approve here.

multisig.cosign.setDiffers.en: The signer set in this request differs from this wallet’s record of the account.

multisig.cosign.notInWallet.en: This account is not in this wallet. Its address was checked against the signer set in the request.

multisig.cosign.notVerified.en: The approval did not verify. Nothing was shared.

multisig.approval.notCollecting.en: This operation is no longer collecting approvals.

multisig.approval.notFound.en: No approval found in the text.

multisig.approval.invalidJson.en: The approval is not valid JSON.

multisig.approval.isRequest.en: This is a signing request, not an approval.

multisig.approval.isRecord.en: This is an account record, not an approval.

multisig.approval.otherNetwork.en: This approval is for another network.

multisig.approval.otherAccount.en: This approval is for another account.

multisig.approval.otherRequest.en: This approval is for another request (a different call or nonce).

multisig.qr.damaged.en: This QR code looks like part of a Shiba Wallet multisig code, but it is damaged. Scan it again.

multisig.qr.tooLarge.en: Too large for QR codes — use Share, Copy or Save as file instead.

multisig.scan.requestRationale.en: Point the camera at the signing request QR code on the submitter’s phone. A request in several parts is read one part at a time.

multisig.scan.approvalRationale.en: Point the camera at the approval QR code on the co-signer’s phone, or at a signature QR code from another wallet.

multisig.scan.recordRationale.en: Point the camera at the multisig record QR code on the other signer’s phone. A record in several parts is read one part at a time.

multisig.scan.requestNote.en: A scanned request is checked exactly like pasted text: the wallet recomputes the account address, the call data and the request id from what it read, and you still see every call in full before anything is signed.

multisig.scan.recordNote.en: A scanned record is checked exactly like pasted text: the account address must follow from its signer set, and one of your recovery-phrase accounts must be a signer.

multisig.scan.approvalNote.en: A scanned approval is checked exactly like pasted text: its signature must recover to a signer of this multisig for this exact request (these calls at this nonce), or it is refused.

multisig.file.chooseJson.en: Choose a .json file exported by Shiba Wallet.

multisig.file.oneObject.en: This file must contain exactly one JSON object and nothing else.

multisig.file.onlyPayloads.en: Only a multisig record, request or approval can be saved as a file.

tokenGas.oracle.baseSepolia.en: On Base Sepolia the paymaster’s test oracle returns a fixed price; it is not a market rate.

tokenGas.oracle.arbitrumSepolia.en: On Arbitrum Sepolia the paymaster’s test oracle returns a fixed price; it is not a market rate.

tokenGas.circle.spreadNote.en: Circle’s documentation mentions a 10% surcharge on Arbitrum and Base; this is the figure the paymaster contract itself reports, and it is the one it charges.

tokenGas.circle.estimateAfterApproval.en: The bundler’s gas estimate runs after you approve, because Circle’s paymaster needs a permit signed by your smart account first. If the estimate fails, nothing is sent.

tokenGas.erc7677.markupValue.en: Included in the rate; not shown as a separate figure

settings.custom.blockTimeNone.en: Block time: not measured, so the warning about recently created contracts is not shown on this network (the rule for every network the wallet has no figure for).

settings.custom.remove.switchesFirst.en: The wallet switches back to Ethereum mainnet first.

settings.custom.remove.kept.en: Kept on this phone: session keys, subscriptions, guardian and inheritance records, passkey details and multi-signature accounts for this chain. They describe things that exist on the network itself, so deleting them would undo nothing there and would remove what you need to revoke or recover them; they come back if you add the same chain id again. Nothing on the network changes.

settings.custom.removed.mainnet.en: The wallet is back on Ethereum mainnet.

settings.custom.removed.nothing.en: No other data was stored for this chain.

settings.customNote.noExplorer.en: No block explorer was given, so the wallet shows no explorer links here.

settings.customNote.testSmart.en: No smart-account deployment is pre-filled (paste a factory under Account Abstraction and the wallet checks it on-chain before saving), swaps are not offered, and tokens start with an empty list.

settings.customNote.defaultRefusal.en: they are switched off there, as on Ethereum mainnet.

settings.protect.subject.oneOf.en: One of your imported private keys

settings.protect.imported.damaged.en: The record of imported private keys on this phone could not be read, so where they are kept is unknown. No key was deleted.

settings.protect.imported.notBackedUp.en: The recovery phrase does not back up imported keys.

settings.protect.unreadable.en: This phone can no longer open your recovery phrase. Its biometric protection was reset (for example, a fingerprint or face was added or removed, or the screen lock was turned off), and the system deletes protected keys when that happens. Nothing was signed and your funds are untouched on-chain. To keep using this wallet here, remove it in Settings and import your written recovery phrase again.

accounts.backupHint.phraseOnly.en: Every account comes from your one recovery phrase — backing up the phrase backs up all of them.

accounts.backupHint.imported.en: Every account except the imported ones comes from your one recovery phrase. Imported accounts are NOT backed up by the phrase: keep their private keys yourself.

sessions.grant.noFunction.en: No contract function: meant for a plain transfer with empty calldata. The account enforces this as function 0x00000000, so a call whose data begins with 0x00000000 would also be allowed. That matters only if the target is a contract.

sessions.grant.perCall.en: The cap is per call, not a total: the session may repeat this call until it expires.

sessions.grant.noteApprove.en: Lets the session approve ANY spender for ANY amount of this token (ERC-20) or any token id (ERC-721). An approval outlives the session.

sessions.grant.noteTransferFrom.en: Moves tokens from any address that approved your account, to any recipient.

sessions.grant.noteApprovalForAll.en: Lets the session give an operator control of ALL your NFTs in this collection. It outlives the session.

sessions.grant.noMessages.en: A session key can never sign messages or logins for your account (ERC-1271 is switched off for it).

sessions.holder.merchant.en: the merchant once you hand it over; until then, this device’s secure storage

sessions.holder.phoneOnly.en: this phone’s secure storage only, never shown or exported

sessions.recurring.review.keyCannotSign.en: The payment key cannot sign messages, logins or permits for your account.

sessions.recurring.review.missed.en: Missed payments are not lost: a payment whose period passed while the wallet was closed can still be sent later, even right before the next one, until the end date.

sessions.recurring.review.keyLives.en: The payment key lives in this phone’s secure storage. Wiping the wallet or restoring it from the recovery phrase deletes it: payments then stop, while the permission stays on-chain until its end date. Revoke before wiping.

sessions.recurring.review.stop.en: Stop at any time with Revoke (one operation signed by your account key). Payments already sent are not returned.

dca.review.keyLives.en: The swap key lives in this phone’s secure storage. Wiping the wallet or restoring it from the recovery phrase deletes it: swaps then stop, while the permission stays on-chain until its end date. Revoke before wiping.

staking.contract.rocketPoolDeposit.en: Rocket Pool deposit pool (resolved from RocketStorage just now)

staking.contract.lidoStakeWrap.en: Lido wstETH contract (stake and wrap in one step)

settings.pinCost.nativeStop.en: This build hashes with native scrypt (react-native-quick-crypto), which cannot be interrupted inside one hash: Stop and the 120-second limit take effect between sizes, and a size already running finishes first.

settings.pinCost.failed.en: The measurement could not be run. Nothing was stored.

activity.note.privacy.en: Notes are kept on this phone and are not sent anywhere. They are deleted when the wallet is wiped. A records backup (Settings → Records backup) includes them, and your recovery phrase restores them from it. Hide amounts does not hide them.

notice.watchOnly.before: Watch-only: this wallet can show this address but holds no key for it. It cannot send, sign or recover anything for it.
notice.watchOnly.en: Watch-only: this wallet can show this address but holds no key for it, so it cannot sign, swap or recover anything for it. A send on an Ethereum network can still be prepared with "Send with an off-line signer" and signed by an off-line signer that holds its key.
notice.watchOnly.why: Phase 22 pass p22a: the off-line signer screen (cold signing, phase 22 item 3) lets a watch-only account prepare a send for an off-line signer, and that screen showed this notice directly above "You can still prepare a send here", so "It cannot send" was no longer true; the wallet still cannot sign, swap or recover for the address.

readiness.bridge.reason.en: A bridge provider’s contracts and verifiers hold your coins while they move: on the test networks each LayerZero route through Stargate is checked by a single verifier operated by LayerZero Labs, and Stargate’s test pools can be paused by a key whose private part is public. Circle’s USDC transfers rest on Circle’s own two attesters and on Circle’s power to pause them, refuse addresses and replace the contracts; this wallet has sent two Circle CCTP Standard Transfers on the test networks, by script (Base Sepolia to Arbitrum Sepolia, and Ethereum Sepolia to Base Sepolia). This wallet offers bridging only on test networks, and its bridge path has not been tested as a real build on real phones.
readiness.bridge.reason.why: Phase 23 item 4: Circle CCTP V2 Standard Transfers were sent live on the test networks by script on 2026-10-25 (docs/BRIDGING.md section 17), and the Bridge screen now offers USDC through CCTP, so "this wallet has not yet sent one" was no longer true; the reason also names Circle’s power to pause, refuse addresses and replace the contracts.
